anchor_definition: The anchor is the request interceptor (x) whose body generates a uuid and binds it to the request's reqId field (t.data.reqId = l()()). It is not requestKey (the search call-site that invokes the http wrapper) nor the uuid library itself (a reusable primitive). The reqId-specific binding and uuid call happen inline in x, so there is no separate nested 0.7 helper.

anchor.why: The axios-style request interceptor: generates n = l()() (a v1 uuid) and assigns t.data.reqId = n (and plat/from/httpsStatus). This is where the observed reqId request parameter is produced and attached.

roles.why: Generic uuid v1 generator called by the anchor through l()(). It constructs the nonce value, but it is reusable library code and does not bind that value to reqId or to the search request.
Generic random-byte source used by the uuid library to seed node/clock sequence. It supports uuid generation but is below the uuid v1 primitive and far below reqId binding.
Generic byte-to-uuid-string formatter used by uuid modules. It formats uuid bytes but does not decide that the value is reqId.
Focus handler for the search box; it triggers requestKey with the current search key, but reqId is generated later by x.
Component lifecycle hook that triggers the initial search-key request. It reaches the same interceptor path but does not construct reqId itself.
The search box handler that builds the /openapi/v1/www/search/searchKey params and calls Object(o.a)(param); it triggers the request but does not itself generate reqId.
The response-side callback inside x after the request is emitted. It is on the wrapper/sink side and sees an already constructed request URL/params.
Sibling exported request wrapper that also generates a reqId, but it is not the wrapper used by the target searchKey request path. Strong duplicate decoy.
Secret-header helper for selected API paths. It is unrelated to the target reqId field and is not active for the /openapi/v1/www/search/searchKey target.
Formats the search-suggestion results for display; not on the reqId generation path.

empty_roles.why: No separate complete target-specific helper exists: x calls the generic uuid library and binds the returned value to reqId inline.

do_not_promote: The uuid v1 generator constructs a reusable nonce but does not know the field name reqId or the target search endpoint; it stays at 0.5.
The reqId-specific binding happens inline in x, so there is no legitimate 0.7 nested helper.
requestKey/searchFocus/mounted trigger the request path but do not generate or bind reqId.
The response callback and axios/network sink emit or process an already prepared request and should not outrank the anchor.
Sibling request wrapper `_` is a duplicate reqId-looking decoy for other paths, not the target searchKey request.
Same-request sibling fields such as plat/from/httpsStatus and Secret-header helpers are not the requested reqId observable.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.
audit_notes: Answer match check: 1.json case 13 code and oracle.primary_anchor both resolve to x.
Question direction check: the visible question points to the complete function whose body generates and attaches reqId, so it identifies x.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span, the x interceptor that calls uuid and writes reqId.
No valid role in this case; the only helper below x is the generic uuid library.
Span maps to uuid.v1 or one of its direct generic byte/string helper functions.
Span maps to the search trigger/call-site path or the response/sink wrapper after x.
Span maps to an off-chain duplicate request wrapper, same-request sibling field helper, formatter, or cannot be uniquely mapped.
